parties.ourParty: Ono Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. (Ono, as licensee/customer)

plans.note: Look for a consequential-damages waiver and any aggregate cap in Article XVI (Indemnification; Recalls) and at the tail of Article XV (Reps/Warranties, often with a disclaimer) or in Article XVIII General Provisions. Check mutuality and whether carve-outs (indemnity, confidentiality, IP infringement, willful misconduct) are preserved; in-licence deals frequently have a mutual no-consequential-damages clause but no monetary cap.

Article XVI (INDEMNIFICATION; RECALLS) should contain the Array Indemnitees / Ono Indemnitees indemnities and procedure (defined terms Array Indemnitees, Ono Indemnitees, Indemnitee, Indemnitor confirm this). Verify Array indemnifies us for third-party IP infringement arising from the licensed compounds and for its own negligence/willful misconduct and breach, that our indemnity is limited to our Territory commercialization and our breach, and that recall cost allocation in 16.6 does not shift Array-caused defects to us.

Article VIII (CERTAIN COVENANTS) is the likely home of competing-product / field restrictions on Ono; also check Article II grant provisions and definitions of Field, Ono Territory and Product for implied restrictions on developing or selling competing MEK/BRAF inhibitors. Assess scope, duration and territory before treating any restriction as a deviation.

Sourcing exclusivity is most likely in Article IX (Product Manufacturing and Supply) — check whether Ono must purchase all Product requirements exclusively from Array and whether there is any right to manufacture or second-source on supply failure. Also review Article II/2.6 for exclusivity and non-assert style covenants binding us.

No MFN-style pricing term is signalled by the outline; scan Article VI/VII (payments, royalties, Net Sales) and Article IX (supply price) for any obligation on Ono to extend best terms to Array. Mark missing/inapplicable if none, and do not flag MFN language that runs in our favour.

Check Article VIII covenants and the General Provisions block for an employee non-solicit; such clauses are uncommon in this deal type. If present, confirm it is mutual, time-limited (12–24 months) and carves out general advertising.

Article XIII (TERM AND TERMINATION) should contain termination at will by Ono on notice plus termination for breach/insolvency; verify notice length, absence of termination fees, and that Array has no convenience right that would strand our development investment. Cross-check consequences in Article XIV.

Term here is tied to royalty terms (Initial Royalty Term, Secondary Royalty Term, Applicable Regulatory Exclusivity Period) rather than an auto-renewing subscription term; check the term clause in Article XIII and those definitions in Article I. Likely no auto-renewal/price-uplift mechanic to flag.

Article XVII (DISPUTE RESOLUTION) plus the governing-law clause in General Provisions; note the defined term Rules and the 17.3 cross-reference suggesting arbitration. Confirm which law governs (New York/Delaware/California/England & Wales are acceptable) and whether disputes go to arbitration, and record the escalation-to-Senior-Executives step.

Assignment clause sits in General Provisions (Article XVIII); the defined term Change in Control indicates CoC mechanics — check whether Array may terminate or restrict on our change of control and whether Ono may assign to Affiliates and to a successor without consent.

Ownership of Improvements, Joint Inventions/Joint Know-How and Ono Know-How is set by Article I definitions plus Article XI (Patent Prosecution and Enforcement); the Grant-Back License reference in 10.5 and Article XII (Trademarks, incl. Exhibit 12.6 domain names) may assign our-generated IP or data to Array. Verify our Data and Ono Know-How are not assigned outright and that any grant-back is non-exclusive and scoped.

Article II (GRANT OF LICENSE) — confirm the licence to Ono covers the Ono Territory and Field, extends to Affiliates, Sublicensees and Subcontractors, and is not revocable at will (only terminable per Article XIII). Check sublicensing consent conditions and any retained-rights limits in 2.6.

Article VII (PAYMENTS; BOOKS AND RECORDS) and the defined term Auditor point to a royalty audit of Ono's records — check frequency (once per Calendar Year), advance notice, records-retention period, independent auditor confidentiality, and that Array bears audit cost absent a material underpayment threshold.

Look for penalty-style payments payable by Ono — late-payment interest in Article VII, diligence/milestone failure penalties in Article IV or VI. Interest at a commercial rate is not a liquidated-damages deviation; only a genuine penalty for our non-performance would be.

Article XV (REPRESENTATIONS, WARRANTIES AND COVENANTS) — check Array's IP/title, no-third-party-conflict and compliance warranties, any product/manufacturing conformity warranty in Article IX, and the scope of any disclaimer of implied warranties at the end of Article XV.

Insurance obligations, if any, usually sit with the indemnity in Article XVI or in General Provisions; product-liability insurance covenants are common in pharma licences but may be absent here. Confirm before treating as missing, and note this is a licence rather than a data/premises services engagement.

Article IX (supply) for minimum order/forecast commitments and take-or-pay style obligations on Ono, and Article VI plus the redacted milestone tables (sec-1 through sec-8 series) for non-refundable minimum payments. Also check Article V/Diligent Efforts for volume or launch commitments; assess whether an exit (termination for convenience) mitigates.

Article XIV (EFFECT OF TERMINATION) with the defined Wind-down Period should cover sell-off rights, transfer of Regulatory Filings/Data, and return or destruction of Confidential Information (cross-check Article X). Verify we get our Data and regulatory materials back and reasonable transition assistance where Array terminates.
